title: Rigveda 3.52: To Indra
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 3.52: To Indra: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 3.52 is a hymn of 8 verses addressed to Indra. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 3, the family book of Viśvāmitra. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 234r-234v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 3.52.1-4 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 3, varga 17); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 234r
translation.original_text:
1dhā̱nāva̍ntaṁ kara̱mbhiṇa̍m apū̱pava̍ntam u̱kthina̍m | indra̍ prā̱tar ju̍ṣasva naḥ ||
2pu̱ro̱ḻāśa̍m paca̱tya̍ṁ ju̱ṣasve̱ndrā gu̍rasva ca | tubhya̍ṁ ha̱vyāni̍ sisrate ||
3pu̱ro̱ḻāśa̍ṁ ca no̱ ghaso̍ jo̱ṣayā̍se̱ gira̍ś ca naḥ | va̱dhū̱yur i̍va̱ yoṣa̍ṇām ||
4pu̱ro̱ḻāśa̍ṁ sanaśruta prātaḥsā̱ve ju̍ṣasva naḥ | indra̱ kratu̱r hi te̍ bṛ̱han ||
translation.text:
1INDRA, accept at break of day our Soma mixt with roasted corn, With groats with cake, with eulogies.
2Accept, O Indra, and enjoy the well-dressed sacrificial cake: Oblations are poured forth to thee.
3Consume our sacrificial cake, accept the songs of praise we sing, As he who woes accepts his bride.
4Famed from of old, accept the cake at our libation poured at dawn, Forgreat, O Indra, is thy power.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 234r (numbered 44r by the scribe) (OPenn image 235, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 3.51.10 ‹ojasā sutam rādhānām pate›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 234v (numbered 44v by the scribe), begins in RV 3.52.5 ‹-tūrṇi-arthaḥ vṛṣa-yamāṇaḥ upa gīḥ-bhiḥ›. Verses 3.52.1-4 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1dhānāvantam | karambhiṇam | apūpa-vantam | ukthinam | indra | prātaḥ | juṣasva | naḥ
2puroḷāsam | pacatyam | juṣasva | indra | ā | gurasva | ca | tubhyam | havyāni | s israte
3puroḷāsam | ca | naḥ | ghasaḥ | joṣayāse | giraḥ | ca | naḥ | vadhūyuḥ-iva | yoṣaṇām
4puroḷāsam | sana-śruta | prātaḥ-sāve | juṣasva | naḥ | indra | kratuḥ | hi | te | bṛhan

translation.original_ref: RV 3.52.5-8 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 3, varga 17); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 234v
translation.original_text:
5mādhya̍ṁdinasya̱ sava̍nasya dhā̱nāḥ pu̍ro̱ḻāśa̍m indra kṛṣve̱ha cāru̍m | pra yat sto̱tā ja̍ri̱tā tūrṇya̍rtho vṛṣā̱yamā̍ṇa̱ upa̍ gī̱rbhir īṭṭe̍ ||
6tṛ̱tīye̍ dhā̱nāḥ sava̍ne puruṣṭuta puro̱ḻāśa̱m āhu̍tam māmahasva naḥ | ṛ̱bhu̱manta̱ṁ vāja̍vantaṁ tvā kave̱ praya̍svanta̱ upa̍ śikṣema dhī̱tibhi̍ḥ ||
7pū̱ṣa̱ṇvate̍ te cakṛmā kara̱mbhaṁ hari̍vate̱ harya̍śvāya dhā̱nāḥ | a̱pū̱pam a̍ddhi̱ saga̍ṇo ma̱rudbhi̱ḥ soma̍m piba vṛtra̱hā śū̍ra vi̱dvān ||
8prati̍ dhā̱nā bha̍rata̱ tūya̍m asmai puro̱ḻāśa̍ṁ vī̱rata̍māya nṛ̱ṇām | di̱ve-di̍ve sa̱dṛśī̍r indra̱ tubhya̱ṁ vardha̍ntu tvā soma̱peyā̍ya dhṛṣṇo ||
translation.text:
5Let roasted corn of our midday libation, and sacrificial cake here please thee, Indra, What time the lauding singer, keen of purpose and eager as a bull, with hymns implores thee.
6At the third sacrifice, O thou whom many praise, give glory to the roasted corn and holy cake. With offered viands and with songs may we assist thee, Sage, whom Vâja and the R̥ibhus wait upon.
7The groats have we prepared for thee with Pûshan, corn for thee, Lord of Bay Steeds, with thy horses. Eat thou the meal-cake, banded with the Maruts, wise Hero, Vr̥itra-slayer, drink the Soma.
8Bring forth the roasted corn to meet him quickly, cake for the bravest Hero mid the heroes. Indra, may hymns accordant with thee daily strengthen thee, Bold One, for the draught of Soma.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 234v (numbered 44v by the scribe) (OPenn image 236, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 3.52.5 ‹-tūrṇi-arthaḥ vṛṣa-yamāṇaḥ upa gīḥ-bhiḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 235r (numbered 45r by the scribe), begins in RV 3.53.1 ‹gīḥ-bhiḥ iḷiyā madantā›. Verses 3.52.5-8 end on this page; 3.52.5 begins on fol. 234r (numbered 44r by the scribe).
